<!-- Author: Kunru Song -->

This report compares a general one-factor model with a correlated
Core--Peripheral two-factor model for the 18 baseline Trait PSMU items. Mplus 8.7
is the computation engine. R and `MplusAutomation` create the model inputs, run
Mplus, parse and validate the outputs, save the canonical model-result RDA, and
create the final Excel workbook and SVG figures.

The baseline CFA is a supplementary trait-level replication. Its result does
not determine the EMA within-person measurement structure.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
locate_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  current <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  if (!dir.exists(current)) current <- dirname(current)
  repeat {
    if (all(dir.exists(file.path(current, c(
      "Step_1_Descriptive_and_Reliability", "Step_2_Measurement_Models"
    ))))) return(current)
    parent <- dirname(current)
    if (identical(parent, current)) break
    current <- parent
  }
  stop("Could not locate the project from its public Step directories")
}
```

# Mplus-safe variables and item mapping

Mplus receives short unique names (`bs1`--`bs18`). The mapping below is retained
in the result RDA and every extracted table so no item identity is lost.

```{r mplus-variable-map}
mplus_item_names <- paste0("bs", 1:18)

variable_map <- data.frame(
  item_number = 1:18,
  project_variable = baseline_items,
  mplus_variable = toupper(mplus_item_names),
  theoretical_group = ifelse(1:18 <= 6L, "Peripheral", "Core"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

mplus_data <- dat_baseline_cfa[baseline_items]
names(mplus_data) <- mplus_item_names
mplus_data <- as.data.frame(mplus_data)

stopifnot(
  identical(names(mplus_data), mplus_item_names),
  nrow(mplus_data) == 209L,
  !anyNA(mplus_data),
  length(unique(substr(names(mplus_data), 1L, 8L))) == 18L
)

knitr::kable(variable_map)
```

# Model specifications

Both models treat the 1--5 responses as ordered categorical and use Mplus
WLSMV with the Delta parameterization. The first item of each factor is the
marker indicator under the Mplus default identification rule. No item parcel,
correlated residual, cross-loading, or post-hoc modification is added.

```{r model-specifications}
model_specs <- list(
  B1_OneFactor = list(
    label = "B1 One-factor",
    stem = "s2_2_1_b1_one_factor",
    title = "S2.2.1 WLSMV B1 one-factor baseline Trait PSMU CFA;",
    model = "trait BY bs1-bs18;"
  ),
  B2_CorePeripheral = list(
    label = "B2 Core-Peripheral",
    stem = "s2_2_1_b2_core_peripheral",
    title = "S2.2.1 WLSMV B2 correlated Core-Peripheral baseline Trait PSMU CFA;",
    model = paste(
      "periph BY bs1-bs6;",
      "core BY bs7-bs18;",
      "periph WITH core;",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  )
)

model_plan <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(model_specs), function(model_id) {
  specification <- model_specs[[model_id]]
  data.frame(
    model_id = model_id,
    model_label = specification$label,
    estimator = "WLSMV",
    parameterization = "DELTA",
    indicator_treatment = "Ordered categorical (1-5)",
    categorical_items = 18L,
    factors = ifelse(model_id == "B1_OneFactor", 1L, 2L),
    mplus_input = paste0(specification$stem, ".inp"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

knitr::kable(model_plan)
```

# Generate and run the Mplus 8.7 models

The `.dat`, `.inp`, and `.out` files are regenerated by this Rmd.

```{r run-mplus-models}
run_mplus_cfa <- function(model_id, specification) {
  model_stem <- specification$stem
  data_path <- file.path(mplus_directory, paste0(model_stem, ".dat"))
  input_path <- file.path(mplus_directory, paste0(model_stem, ".inp"))
  output_path <- file.path(mplus_directory, paste0(model_stem, ".out"))

  mplus_object <- MplusAutomation::mplusObject(
    TITLE = paste(
      "! Author: Kunru Song",
      specification$title,
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    VARIABLE = "CATEGORICAL = bs1-bs18;",
    ANALYSIS = paste(
      "ESTIMATOR = WLSMV;",
      "PARAMETERIZATION = DELTA;",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    MODEL = specification$model,
    OUTPUT = paste(
      "SAMPSTAT;",
      "STANDARDIZED(STDYX);",
      "CINTERVAL;",
      "RESIDUAL;",
      "MODINDICES(10);",
      "TECH1;",
      "TECH4;",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    usevariables = mplus_item_names,
    rdata = mplus_data,
    autov = FALSE,
    quiet = TRUE
  )

  modeler_result <- MplusAutomation::mplusModeler(
    object = mplus_object,
    dataout = data_path,
    modelout = input_path,
    run = 1L,
    check = FALSE,
    varwarnings = TRUE,
    Mplus_command = mplus_command,
    writeData = "always",
    hashfilename = FALSE,
    killOnFail = TRUE,
    quiet = TRUE
  )

  if (!file.exists(output_path)) {
    stop("Mplus did not create the expected output: ", output_path)
  }

  input_lines <- readLines(input_path, warn = FALSE)
  output_lines <- readLines(output_path, warn = FALSE)
  author_present <- any(trimws(input_lines) == "! Author: Kunru Song")
  normal_termination <- any(grepl(
    "THE MODEL ESTIMATION TERMINATED NORMALLY",
    output_lines,
    fixed = TRUE
  ))

  if (!author_present) stop("Missing required author text in: ", input_path)
  if (!normal_termination) stop("Mplus model did not terminate normally: ", output_path)

  parsed <- MplusAutomation::readModels(
    target = output_path,
    what = "all",
    quiet = TRUE
  )

  list(
    model_id = model_id,
    model_label = specification$label,
    model_syntax = specification$model,
    paths = list(data = data_path, input = input_path, output = output_path),
    author_present = author_present,
    normal_termination = normal_termination,
    parsed = parsed,
    modeler_result = modeler_result
  )
}

model_runs <- lapply(names(model_specs), function(model_id) {
  run_mplus_cfa(model_id, model_specs[[model_id]])
})
names(model_runs) <- names(model_specs)
```

# Validate parsed Mplus output

Technical admissibility is evaluated separately from global model fit. Poor fit
does not cause a technically valid model run to be discarded.

```{r validate-mplus-output}
flatten_messages <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0L) return(NA_character_)
  values <- unlist(x, recursive = TRUE, use.names = FALSE)
  values <- trimws(as.character(values))
  values <- values[nzchar(values)]
  if (!length(values)) NA_character_ else paste(unique(values), collapse = " | ")
}

extract_loading_rows <- function(parsed) {
  standard <- parsed$parameters$stdyx.standardized
  standard[grepl("\\.BY$", standard$paramHeader), , drop = FALSE]
}

extract_factor_correlation_rows <- function(parsed) {
  standard <- parsed$parameters$stdyx.standardized
  standard[grepl("\\.WITH$", standard$paramHeader), , drop = FALSE]
}

technical_diagnostics <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(model_runs, function(run) {
  parsed <- run$parsed
  summary_row <- parsed$summaries[1, , drop = FALSE]
  loading_rows <- extract_loading_rows(parsed)
  factor_correlation_rows <- extract_factor_correlation_rows(parsed)
  r2_rows <- parsed$parameters$r2

  version_ok <- identical(as.character(summary_row$Mplus.version), "8.7")
  estimator_ok <- identical(as.character(summary_row$Estimator), "WLSMV")
  observations_ok <- identical(as.integer(summary_row$Observations), 209L)
  errors_n <- length(parsed$errors)
  warnings_n <- length(parsed$warnings)
  loadings_admissible <- all(is.finite(loading_rows$est)) &&
    all(abs(loading_rows$est) <= 1.001)
  residuals_admissible <- !is.null(r2_rows) &&
    all(is.finite(r2_rows$resid_var)) &&
    all(r2_rows$resid_var >= -0.001)
  correlations_admissible <- !nrow(factor_correlation_rows) ||
    all(abs(factor_correlation_rows$est) < 1)

  data.frame(
    model_id = run$model_id,
    model = run$model_label,
    mplus_version = as.character(summary_row$Mplus.version),
    estimator = as.character(summary_row$Estimator),
    observations = as.integer(summary_row$Observations),
    normal_termination = run$normal_termination,
    author_present = run$author_present,
    errors_n = errors_n,
    warnings_n = warnings_n,
    errors = flatten_messages(parsed$errors),
    warnings = flatten_messages(parsed$warnings),
    maximum_absolute_loading = max(abs(loading_rows$est)),
    minimum_residual_variance = min(r2_rows$resid_var),
    maximum_absolute_factor_correlation = if (nrow(factor_correlation_rows)) {
      max(abs(factor_correlation_rows$est))
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    version_ok = version_ok,
    estimator_ok = estimator_ok,
    observations_ok = observations_ok,
    loadings_admissible = loadings_admissible,
    residuals_admissible = residuals_admissible,
    correlations_admissible = correlations_admissible,
    technical_checks_passed = all(c(
      run$normal_termination,
      run$author_present,
      version_ok,
      estimator_ok,
      observations_ok,
      errors_n == 0L,
      loadings_admissible,
      residuals_admissible,
      correlations_admissible
    )),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

if (!all(technical_diagnostics$technical_checks_passed)) {
  stop(
    "At least one Mplus CFA failed technical validation: ",
    paste(
      technical_diagnostics$model[!technical_diagnostics$technical_checks_passed],
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}

knitr::kable(technical_diagnostics, digits = 3)
```

# Extract fit and parameter results

```{r extract-results}
extract_fit <- function(run) {
  summary_row <- run$parsed$summaries[1, , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(
    model_id = run$model_id,
    model = run$model_label,
    mplus_version = as.character(summary_row$Mplus.version),
    estimator = as.character(summary_row$Estimator),
    parameterization = "DELTA",
    n = as.integer(summary_row$Observations),
    free_parameters = as.integer(summary_row$Parameters),
    chi_square = as.numeric(summary_row$ChiSqM_Value),
    df = as.integer(summary_row$ChiSqM_DF),
    p_value = as.numeric(summary_row$ChiSqM_PValue),
    cfi = as.numeric(summary_row$CFI),
    tli = as.numeric(summary_row$TLI),
    rmsea = as.numeric(summary_row$RMSEA_Estimate),
    rmsea_90ci_lower = as.numeric(summary_row$RMSEA_90CI_LB),
    rmsea_90ci_upper = as.numeric(summary_row$RMSEA_90CI_UB),
    rmsea_p_close = as.numeric(summary_row$RMSEA_pLT05),
    srmr = as.numeric(summary_row$SRMR),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

model_fit <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(model_runs, extract_fit)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    delta_cfi_vs_b1 = c(NA_real_, cfi[2] - cfi[1]),
    delta_tli_vs_b1 = c(NA_real_, tli[2] - tli[1]),
    delta_rmsea_vs_b1 = c(NA_real_, rmsea[2] - rmsea[1]),
    delta_srmr_vs_b1 = c(NA_real_, srmr[2] - srmr[1])
  )

extract_loadings <- function(run) {
  parsed <- run$parsed
  standard <- extract_loading_rows(parsed)
  standard_ci <- parsed$parameters$ci.stdyx.standardized
  standard_ci <- standard_ci[
    grepl("\\.BY$", standard_ci$paramHeader),
    c("paramHeader", "param", "low2.5", "up2.5"),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  unstandard <- parsed$parameters$unstandardized
  unstandard <- unstandard[
    grepl("\\.BY$", unstandard$paramHeader),
    c("paramHeader", "param", "est", "se"),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  names(unstandard)[3:4] <- c("unstandardized_loading", "unstandardized_se")
  r2 <- parsed$parameters$r2[, c("param", "est", "resid_var"), drop = FALSE]
  names(r2)[2] <- "r_squared"

  result <- standard |>
    dplyr::select(
      paramHeader,
      param,
      standardized_loading = est,
      standardized_se = se,
      standardized_z = est_se,
      standardized_p = pval
    ) |>
    dplyr::left_join(standard_ci, by = c("paramHeader", "param")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(unstandard, by = c("paramHeader", "param")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(r2, by = "param") |>
    dplyr::left_join(variable_map, by = c("param" = "mplus_variable")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      model_id = run$model_id,
      model = run$model_label,
      factor = sub("\\.BY$", "", paramHeader),
      standardized_ci_lower = low2.5,
      standardized_ci_upper = up2.5
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(
      model_id,
      model,
      factor,
      item_number,
      project_variable,
      theoretical_group,
      unstandardized_loading,
      unstandardized_se,
      standardized_loading,
      standardized_se,
      standardized_z,
      standardized_p,
      standardized_ci_lower,
      standardized_ci_upper,
      r_squared,
      residual_variance = resid_var
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(item_number)

  result
}

loadings <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(model_runs, extract_loadings))

extract_factor_correlation <- function(run) {
  standard <- extract_factor_correlation_rows(run$parsed)
  if (!nrow(standard)) return(NULL)

  standard_ci <- run$parsed$parameters$ci.stdyx.standardized
  standard_ci <- standard_ci[
    grepl("\\.WITH$", standard_ci$paramHeader),
    c("paramHeader", "param", "low2.5", "up2.5"),
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  standard |>
    dplyr::select(
      paramHeader,
      param,
      correlation = est,
      se,
      z = est_se,
      p_value = pval
    ) |>
    dplyr::left_join(standard_ci, by = c("paramHeader", "param")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      model_id = run$model_id,
      model = run$model_label,
      factor_1 = sub("\\.WITH$", "", paramHeader),
      factor_2 = param,
      correlation = correlation,
      se = se,
      z = z,
      p_value = p_value,
      ci_lower = low2.5,
      ci_upper = up2.5
    )
}

factor_correlations <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(model_runs, extract_factor_correlation))

loading_summary <- loadings |>
  dplyr::group_by(model_id, model, factor) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    items = dplyr::n(),
    minimum_standardized_loading = min(standardized_loading),
    mean_standardized_loading = mean(standardized_loading),
    maximum_standardized_loading = max(standardized_loading),
    minimum_r_squared = min(r_squared),
    maximum_r_squared = max(r_squared),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(model_fit, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(loading_summary, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(factor_correlations, digits = 3)
```

# Save the canonical parsed model-result RDA

```{r save-model-result}
project_root_normalized <- normalizePath(project_root, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

make_relative_path <- function(path) {
  normalized <- normalizePath(path, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  root_prefix <- paste0(project_root_normalized, "/")
  if (startsWith(normalized, root_prefix)) {
    substring(normalized, nchar(root_prefix) + 1L)
  } else {
    normalized
  }
}

mplus_file_manifest <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(model_runs, function(run) {
  data.frame(
    model_id = run$model_id,
    model = run$model_label,
    file_type = c("data", "input", "output"),
    relative_path = vapply(run$paths, make_relative_path, character(1)),
    md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(unlist(run$paths))),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
```

# Export the final result workbook in R

```{r export-workbook}
round_numeric_columns <- function(data, digits = 4L) {
  data |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, digits))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.factor), as.character))
}

workbook_sheets <- list(
  Model_Fit = round_numeric_columns(model_fit),
  Loadings = round_numeric_columns(loadings),
  Factor_Correlation = round_numeric_columns(factor_correlations),
  Diagnostics = round_numeric_columns(technical_diagnostics)
)

bruceR::export(
  workbook_sheets,
  file = table_file,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# Apply a reproducible scientific-results format in R after the required
# bruceR export. This preserves typed numeric cells while improving reviewability.
workbook <- openxlsx::loadWorkbook(table_file)
header_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(
  fontName = "Arial",
  fontSize = 10,
  fontColour = "#FFFFFF",
  fgFill = "#1F4E78",
  textDecoration = "bold",
  halign = "center",
  valign = "center",
  wrapText = TRUE,
  border = "bottom",
  borderColour = "#163A5C"
)
decimal_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(numFmt = "0.000")
integer_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(numFmt = "#,##0")

integer_column_names <- c(
  "n",
  "df",
  "free_parameters",
  "item_number",
  "errors_n",
  "warnings_n",
  "observations"
)

for (sheet_name in names(workbook_sheets)) {
  sheet_data <- workbook_sheets[[sheet_name]]
  n_rows <- nrow(sheet_data)
  n_columns <- ncol(sheet_data)

  openxlsx::addStyle(
    workbook,
    sheet = sheet_name,
    style = header_style,
    rows = 1,
    cols = seq_len(n_columns),
    gridExpand = TRUE,
    stack = TRUE
  )
  openxlsx::setRowHeights(workbook, sheet_name, rows = 1, heights = 30)
  openxlsx::freezePane(workbook, sheet_name, firstRow = TRUE)
  openxlsx::addFilter(workbook, sheet_name, rows = 1, cols = seq_len(n_columns))
  openxlsx::showGridLines(workbook, sheet_name, showGridLines = FALSE)

  column_widths <- vapply(seq_len(n_columns), function(column_index) {
    values <- c(names(sheet_data)[column_index], as.character(sheet_data[[column_index]]))
    values[is.na(values)] <- ""
    min(38, max(10, max(nchar(values), na.rm = TRUE) + 2))
  }, numeric(1))
  openxlsx::setColWidths(
    workbook,
    sheet = sheet_name,
    cols = seq_len(n_columns),
    widths = column_widths
  )

  if (n_rows > 0L) {
    numeric_columns <- which(vapply(sheet_data, is.numeric, logical(1)))
    integer_columns <- which(names(sheet_data) %in% integer_column_names)
    decimal_columns <- setdiff(numeric_columns, integer_columns)

    if (length(integer_columns)) {
      openxlsx::addStyle(
        workbook,
        sheet = sheet_name,
        style = integer_style,
        rows = 2:(n_rows + 1L),
        cols = integer_columns,
        gridExpand = TRUE,
        stack = TRUE
      )
    }
    if (length(decimal_columns)) {
      openxlsx::addStyle(
        workbook,
        sheet = sheet_name,
        style = decimal_style,
        rows = 2:(n_rows + 1L),
        cols = decimal_columns,
        gridExpand = TRUE,
        stack = TRUE
      )
    }
  }
}

openxlsx::saveWorkbook(workbook, table_file, overwrite = TRUE)

# openxlsx can retain orphan drawing relationships introduced by the original
# bruceR workbook even though no drawing parts are present. Excel tolerates
# them, but stricter OOXML readers do not. Remove only those two orphan
# relationship types, leaving worksheet data, styles, and printer settings
# unchanged.
repair_orphan_drawing_relationships <- function(xlsx_file) {
  repair_dir <- tempfile("baseline_cfa_xlsx_repair_")
  dir.create(repair_dir)
  on.exit(unlink(repair_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE), add = TRUE)

  members <- utils::unzip(xlsx_file, list = TRUE)$Name
  # Reject unsafe archive paths before extracting a package.
  unsafe_member <- function(path) {
    parts <- strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "/", path), "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    grepl("^[/\\\\]|^[A-Za-z]:", path) || any(parts == "..")
  }
  stopifnot(length(members) > 0L, !anyDuplicated(members),
            !any(vapply(members, unsafe_member, logical(1))))
  utils::unzip(xlsx_file, exdir = repair_dir)
  relationship_files <- list.files(
    file.path(repair_dir, "xl", "worksheets", "_rels"),
    pattern = "\\.rels$", full.names = TRUE
  )
  if (!length(relationship_files)) return(invisible(0L))

  resolve_member <- function(target) {
    target <- gsub("\\\\", "/", utils::URLdecode(target))
    if (!nzchar(target) || grepl("^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:", target)) {
      stop("Invalid internal drawing target")
    }
    parts <- strsplit(target, "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    result <- if (startsWith(target, "/")) character() else c("xl", "worksheets")
    for (part in parts) {
      if (!nzchar(part) || part == ".") next
      if (part == "..") {
        if (!length(result)) stop("Drawing target escapes the workbook package")
        result <- head(result, -1L)
      } else result <- c(result, part)
    }
    paste(result, collapse = "/")
  }
  drawing_types <- paste0(
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/",
    c("drawing", "vmlDrawing")
  )
  removed_relationships <- 0L
  for (relationship_file in relationship_files) {
    document <- xml2::read_xml(relationship_file, options = "NONET")
    relationships <- xml2::xml_find_all(
      document, "/*[local-name()='Relationships']/*[local-name()='Relationship']"
    )
    changed <- FALSE
    for (relationship in relationships) {
      type <- xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "Type")
      external <- identical(xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "TargetMode"), "External")
      if (!type %in% drawing_types || external) next
      target <- xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "Target")
      if (is.na(target)) stop("Drawing relationship is missing its Target")
      if (!resolve_member(target) %in% members) {
        xml2::xml_remove(relationship)
        removed_relationships <- removed_relationships + 1L
        changed <- TRUE
      }
    }
    if (changed) xml2::write_xml(document, relationship_file)
  }
  if (removed_relationships == 0L) return(invisible(0L))

  repaired_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
  on.exit(unlink(repaired_file), add = TRUE)
  archive_members <- list.files(
    repair_dir, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE
  )
  zip::zipr(
    zipfile = repaired_file, files = archive_members, root = repair_dir,
    include_directories = FALSE, mode = "mirror"
  )
  stopifnot(file.exists(repaired_file), file.info(repaired_file)$size > 0)
  stopifnot(file.copy(repaired_file, xlsx_file, overwrite = TRUE))
  invisible(removed_relationships)
}

orphan_relationships_removed <- repair_orphan_drawing_relationships(table_file)

stopifnot(
  file.exists(table_file),
  identical(
    openxlsx::getSheetNames(table_file),
    names(workbook_sheets)
  )
)
```

# Visualize model fit and standardized loadings in R

Reference lines indicate conventional fit guidelines; model selection also requires substantive and diagnostic assessment.

```{r create-fit-figure}
fit_plot_data <- model_fit |>
  dplyr::select(model, cfi, tli, rmsea, srmr) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cfi, tli, rmsea, srmr),
    names_to = "fit_index",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    fit_index = factor(
      fit_index,
      levels = c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr"),
      labels = c("CFI", "TLI", "RMSEA", "SRMR")
    ),
    model = factor(
      model,
      levels = c("B1 One-factor", "B2 Core-Peripheral")
    )
  )

fit_references <- data.frame(
  fit_index = factor(
    c("CFI", "TLI", "RMSEA", "SRMR"),
    levels = c("CFI", "TLI", "RMSEA", "SRMR")
  ),
  reference = c(.95, .95, .06, .08)
)

fit_figure <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  fit_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = model, y = value, color = model)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    data = fit_references,
    ggplot2::aes(yintercept = reference),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey45",
    linewidth = .5
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", value)),
    vjust = -1,
    show.legend = FALSE,
    size = 3.3
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ fit_index, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(.05, .18))) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("#4C78A8", "#E45756")) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Baseline Trait PSMU CFA model fit",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines are conventional descriptive references",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Fit-index value",
    color = "Model"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = fit_figure_file,
  plot = fit_figure,
  device = "svg",
  width = 10,
  height = 4.8,
  units = "in",
  bg = "white"
)
```

# Interpretation

```{r validation-checks, include=FALSE}
artifact_manifest <- data.frame(
  role = c(
    "Parsed model-result RDA",
    "Final result workbook",
    "Model-fit SVG",
    "Standardized-loading SVG"
  ),
  relative_path = c(
    "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis/fit_s2_2_1_baseline_cfa_wlsmv.rda",
    "Res_3_Results/Table_S2_2_1_BaselineCFA_PSMU18items_WLSMV.xlsx",
    "Res_3_Results/Figure_S2_2_1_BaselineCFA_PSMU18items_WLSMV_Fit.svg",
    "Res_3_Results/Figure_S2_2_1_BaselineCFA_PSMU18items_WLSMV_Loadings.svg"
  ),

    loading_figure_file
  )),
  bytes = file.info(c(

    table_file,
    fit_figure_file,

  ))$size,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  all(artifact_manifest$exists),
  all(artifact_manifest$bytes > 0),
  all(technical_diagnostics$technical_checks_passed),
  all(model_fit$n == 209L),
  nrow(loadings) == 36L,
  nrow(factor_correlations) == 1L
)


```

Both models were estimated by Mplus 8.7 with WLSMV and passed the prespecified
technical checks. The one-factor model had CFI =
`r sprintf("%.3f", model_fit$cfi[model_fit$model_id == "B1_OneFactor"])`, TLI =
`r sprintf("%.3f", model_fit$tli[model_fit$model_id == "B1_OneFactor"])`, RMSEA =
`r sprintf("%.3f", model_fit$rmsea[model_fit$model_id == "B1_OneFactor"])`, and
SRMR = `r sprintf("%.3f", model_fit$srmr[model_fit$model_id == "B1_OneFactor"])`.
The correlated Core--Peripheral model had CFI =
`r sprintf("%.3f", model_fit$cfi[model_fit$model_id == "B2_CorePeripheral"])`,
TLI = `r sprintf("%.3f", model_fit$tli[model_fit$model_id == "B2_CorePeripheral"])`,
RMSEA = `r sprintf("%.3f", model_fit$rmsea[model_fit$model_id == "B2_CorePeripheral"])`,
and SRMR = `r sprintf("%.3f", model_fit$srmr[model_fit$model_id == "B2_CorePeripheral"])`.
Its standardized Core--Peripheral correlation was
`r sprintf("%.3f", factor_correlations$correlation)` (95% CI
[`r sprintf("%.3f", factor_correlations$ci_lower)`,
`r sprintf("%.3f", factor_correlations$ci_upper)`]).

The two-factor model improves all four reported fit indices relative to the
one-factor model, but its absolute fit remains poor by conventional descriptive
guides. The better relative fit does not establish that the two-factor model fits adequately. This supplementary baseline analysis does not determine the EMA measurement structure. No post-hoc residual correlation or cross-loading was
added after observing the fit.
